title: Naismith, James
creator: Dictionary of Canadian Biography
gloss: Biographical source: born 6 November 1861 in Ramsay Township, Upper Canada; physical instructor at the International YMCA Training School, Springfield, Massachusetts, from 1892; invented an early football headgear in 1891; devised basketball in 1891 with the first game played 21 December 1891 (some sources say the 15th); the 13 rules published in 1892; to the University of Kansas in 1898 as chapel director, coach and head of physical education; full professor 1906; retired June 1937; filed for American citizenship near the end of the First World War, 'which would be granted in 1925'; died 28 November 1939 in Lawrence, Kansas.

title: James Naismith
creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
gloss: Corroborating source: Luther Halsey Gulick set the challenge to devise an indoor winter game at the Springfield YMCA Training School in autumn 1891; peach baskets used as goals; Naismith earned a medical degree in 1898 (Gross Medical College, Denver) and chaired physical education at the University of Kansas.

title: James Naismith
creator: Wikipedia
gloss: Source for two specific facts: Naismith coached basketball at the University of Kansas from 1898 to 1907 with a record of 55-60, described as 'the only coach in the program's history to have a losing record'; and in 1936 the National Association of Basketball Coaches raised funds so he could attend the Berlin Olympics, where basketball made its Olympic debut and he handed out the medals (United States gold, Canada silver, Mexico bronze).
